name: Nice · Côte d'Azur (Ironman 70.3 World Championships September 2026)

places.name: Ironman 70.3 World Championship Finish Arena
places.description: 150m red carpet finish chute, M-Dot arch, timing clocks, dual grandstands, and VIP viewing terrace on Promenade des Anglais.

places.name: Ironman 70.3 Transition Zone (T1 / T2)
places.description: Main transition zone on Quai des États-Unis with 2,500 bike racks, pro staging, change tents, and athlete recovery pavilion.

places.name: Baie des Anges Swim Start & Australian Exit
places.description: Plage des Ponchettes rolling swim start pontoon, timing carpets on the pebble beach, and 1.9km buoy circuit in the Mediterranean.

places.name: Ironman 70.3 World Village & Expo
places.description: Jardin Albert 1er athlete check-in, Canyon Speedmax showcase, official merchandise superstore, and nutrition zone.

places.name: Hôtel Le Negresco
places.description: Legendary Belle Époque palace opened in 1913, featuring the iconic pink dome designed by Édouard Niermans, overlooking the race course.

places.name: Hyatt Regency Nice Palais de la Méditerranée
places.description: Prestigious Art Deco luxury hotel with white marble arcade facade facing the Promenade des Anglais.

places.name: Café du Cycliste
places.description: The world-famous flagship cycling clubhouse & cafe on the Old Port (Port Lympia), providing premium bike rental, mechanics, and specialty espresso.

places.name: SPOC Vélo Nice Pro Mechanic
places.description: High-end triathlon and road race mechanic, certified Shimano and SRAM service center with disc wheel truing and electronic shifting diagnostics.

places.name: Tour Bellanda & Castle Hill Observation Deck
places.description: Historic 16th-century tower perched on Castle Hill cliff, offering the definitive panoramic viewpoint over the entire Baie des Anges.

places.name: Cours Saleya Market & René Socca
places.description: Vibrant pedestrian market with striped awnings, fresh flowers, and authentic Niçois wood-fired chickpea socca for post-race refueling.

places.name: Place Masséna & Fontaine du Soleil
places.description: Nice's iconic central square featuring black-and-white checkerboard paving, red neoclassical Italianate arcades, and the marble Apollo fountain.

places.name: Port Lympia (Old Port of Nice)
places.description: Historic Mediterranean port basin with Venetian-shuttered facades, luxury yachts, and traditional wooden pointu fishing vessels.

places.name: Aéroport Nice Côte d'Azur (NCE / LFMN)
places.description: France's 2nd busiest international gateway with its famous offshore reclaimed runway peninsula (Runways 04L/22R and 04R/22L) jutting into the sea.

places.name: Col de Vence & Hinterland Bike Climb
places.description: Iconic 90km bike course summit at 963m elevation with limestone karst switchbacks and panoramic views over the entire French Riviera.

places.name: Monoprix Garibaldi (Athlete Fuel & Groceries)
places.description: Major central supermarket near Place Garibaldi with organic produce, electrolyte waters, carb-loading staples, and athlete supplies.

places.name: Castel Plage Waterfront Club
places.description: Exclusive seaside dining and private pebble beach nestled right below the sheer limestone cliffs of Castle Hill.

places.name: Les Chaises Bleues de la Promenade
places.description: The world-famous blue chairs designed by Jean-Michel Wilmotte and Charles Tordo, lining the promenade edge facing the Mediterranean.

places.name: Cascade du Château Waterfall
places.description: Majestic 18th-century artificial waterfall tumbling down the rock faces of Castle Hill above the Old Town roofs.
